title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
In the UK in the period January to March (Q1) 2026:

Box office revenue was £244 million, up 5% on Q1 2025.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
There were 30 million cinema admissions, up 7% on Q1 2025.
Figures are for all films on release, including event releases and those that started their release prior to the Q1 period.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
January recorded Q1 2026’s highest monthly admissions, at 11 million.
The Housemaid, Avatar: Fire & Ash and Hamnet were the highest earning releases of that month.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
At the UK and Republic of Ireland (ROI) box office:

Revenue for films released in Q1 2026 was £199 million, up 6% on Q1 2025.
This excludes event releases.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: The total market share of all UK qualifying films was 57.4%, approximately 3 percentage points higher than Q1 2025’s UK qualifying share.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
In the UK, in the 12 months to March 2026:

The combined total spend on film and high-end television (HETV) production was £6.51 billion, up 5% on the previous 12-month period.
This graph shows the figures that were ‘first reported’ for production spend in each 12-month period.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
Production data is revised every period to account for lags in obtaining complete data across all types of productions.
Combined spend for the 12 months to March 2026 was down 2% on revised figures for the previous 12-month period.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: HETV accounted for 58% of UK production spend in the 12 months to March 2026.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: UK spend on film production was £2.73 billion for the 12 months ending March 2026, up 0% compared with revised figures for the 12 months ending March 2025.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
The BFI assigns productions to one of three categories:

Inward investment features (INW)
Domestic UK features (DOM)
Co-productions (COP)

See notes to statistics releases for full definitions.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: UK spend on HETV projects was £3.78 billion in the 12 months to March 2026, down 4% on revised figures for the previous 12-month period.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: Spend on co-productions almost doubled compared with revised figures for the 12 months to March 2025.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
In the UK, in the 12 months to March 2026:

Combined production starts were down 8% on first reported figures for the 12 months to March 2025.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: Production count for the 12 months to March 2026 is lower than for the other periods shown here. However, as previously noted, figures are likely to be revised upward in subsequent statistical releases as more data becomes available.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: We saw earlier that HETV accounted for the majority of UK production spend in the 12 months to March 2026. In terms of number of productions, however, film accounted for the majority: 52%.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: 186 films were recorded as starting principal photography in the UK in the 12 months to March 2026.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: Lags in obtaining complete data on production activity tend to disproportionately affect counts for domestic UK feature films (DOM), particularly those with budgets of less than £500,000.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: 173 HETV programmes were recorded as starting principal photography in the UK in the 12 months to March 2026.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: HETV programme starts in the 12 months to March 2026 included 13 feature-length single episode productions.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
In the 12 months to March 2026:

A total of 604 films received final certification, either under the cultural test or as an official co-production.
Certification is required to access UK tax reliefs and credits for audiovisual and video game expenditure.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
Films achieving final certification in the 12 months to March 2026 had an associated UK production spend of £2.69 billion.
Films and other productions can apply for final certification when they have completed production and are ready to be released.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
252 HETV titles received final certification through the cultural test in the 12 months to March 2026.
There were two co-productions with final certification but details are not included for disclosure control reasons.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: HETV productions receiving final certification under the cultural test in the 12 months to March 2026 had a UK production spend of £4.62 billion.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
70 animation television programmes received final certification under the cultural test in the 12 months to March 2026.
There were two co-productions with final certification but details are not included for disclosure control reasons.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: Animation TV productions receiving final certification under the cultural test in the 12 months to March 2026 had a UK production spend of £212 million.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
80 children’s television programmes received final certification under the cultural test in the 12 months to March 2026.
There was one co-production with final certification but details are not included for disclosure control reasons.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: Children’s TV productions receiving final certification under the cultural test in the 12 months to March 2026 had a UK production spend of £203 million.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text:
318 video games received final certification in the 12 months to March 2026.
Video games can only be certified under the cultural test.

title: Screen sector statistics to March 2026
text: Video games receiving final certification in the 12 months to March 2026 had a UK production spend of £1.06 billion.
